pr.title: Publish and list review suggestions through the CLI
pr.head: 9e82443c5be958577236734d351cd643ab13f4a7

summary: Projector's review loop publishes each review of a pull request through project review publish. A review sorts what it finds by priority. P1 and P2 findings become inline threads that block the pull request. P3 items, called suggestions, are changes the code is correct without. They never block, but the fix-pr skill must implement or defer each one.

Until now the reviewing agent typed the suggestions section into the review body by hand, and it came out as ## Suggestions, ### Suggestions, a bold line, or a plain Suggestions: line. fix-pr was told to look for one of those forms, so it missed suggestions written in another. This pull request moves both ends of the job into the CLI:

1. Writing. publish takes suggestions as P3 entries in its threads file, ends the body with one canonical ### Suggestions list, and records the count in the review's marker comment as suggestions=N.
  2. Reading. A new project review suggestions command parses the canonical list and every hand-written form, and fix-pr now takes its suggestions from that command instead of reading review bodies.
  3. Counting. project review status and the watch loop's REVIEW line show how many suggestions a review lists.
The skills change to match: review-pr and its method stop telling the reviewer to write the section, and fix-pr calls the new command.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Review marker: the hidden <!-- projector-review v=1 … --> HTML comment on the second line of every Projector review. Every Projector reader, such as status, publish, and the site, finds a review's verdict through it.
  • Incremental review: a short clean review of a small push. It lists no suggestions of its own and links the full review it builds on.
  • Threads file: the JSON list of findings an agent passes to publish --threads.

cards.title: Review status at 9e82443
cards.html:
The Projector review of 9e82443 requests changes, with one P2 thread. The new suggestions= field sits inside the review marker. Every earlier release matches that marker with a pattern that ends at covered=… -->, so an earlier release reads any review this release publishes as no verdict at all. The flag on src/projector/review.py line 1929 has the details.

The gate passed: 1079 tests OK with 1 skipped, plus project check and both plugin validations.

groups.title: The CLI writes, reads, and counts suggestions
groups.kicker: publish lists P3 entries in one form; review suggestions and review status read them back
intro: All of the behavior lives in src/projector/review.py. A review's marker is the hidden HTML comment that carries its verdict, the head it judged, and its counts. A P3 entry is an item in the threads file with "priority": "P3". It names a file, optionally a line, and the suggestion in its body.

1. Publish. suggestion_entries checks each P3 entry. check_threads skips P3 entries, so they need no diff line, and they are removed before the comments go out, so they open no thread and findings= excludes them. compose appends suggestions_section and writes the count into the marker. A body that already has a hand-written section publishes unchanged, with its items counted, unless P3 entries are given too. In that case publish refuses, because the list would appear twice.
  2. Read. parse_suggestions finds the first suggestions label outside fenced code, and treats each list item after it as one suggestion until the next heading, bold line, Label: line, or new paragraph. suggestions applies it to each model's newest review of the head and, for an incremental review, to the full review its lead links.
  3. Count. newest_verdicts gives each verdict a suggestions count, taken from the marker or else from the body. After an incremental review, the count includes the full review's suggestions.

files.note: Marker grammar, P3 entries in publish, the section writer and parser, and the suggestions and status readers.

checks.text: Every marker now ends with suggestions=N, even when N is 0. MARKER in every earlier release ends at covered=<n>/<n> -->. Projector 0.7.19's own verdict_marker returns None for such a marker. So an older status prints unreviewed on a head this release signed off, an older publish ignores this release's verdict when it sets draft state, and a site built at an older action ref shows the head as Unreviewed. The incremental-review plan put the incremental head on a line of its own to avoid this hazard. Open review thread.

Ran parse_suggestions at this head on the bodies of 28 Projector reviews from #300 to #325. It found every listed item in the ##, ###, and plain Suggestions: forms, and stopped at each What was checked or Checked: label.
A P3 body with several lines, a code span holding a colon, or text opening with 1. round-trips through suggestions_section and parse_suggestions unchanged.

A hand-written section ends at any line that looks like Label:. An intro line such as Two small things: right after the heading therefore ends the section before its list. The canonical form publish writes never has such a line.
FULL_REVIEW_LINK matches the sentence incremental_lead writes, and both it and verdicts use the review's html_url, so the incremental review's link finds the full review.

groups.title: The watch loop says how many suggestions a review lists
groups.kicker: The REVIEW line gains a count read from the review marker
intro: The watch loop's script polls tracked pull requests and prints a REVIEW line for each review body with no inline thread. A clean Projector review can still carry suggestions for fix-pr, so the line now ends with , listing 2 suggestions when the review's marker counts any. A review published by an earlier release has no count, and its line names none.

files.note: Captures suggestions=N from the marker as a new tab-separated field and prints it in the REVIEW line.

checks.text: jq's capture gives no output on a body without the field, so // "0" applies. The new field is never empty, so read still puts the snippet in csnip. test_a_projector_review_says_how_many_suggestions_its_marker_counts passes.

files.note: Describes the count on the REVIEW line.

groups.title: The skills hand suggestions to the CLI
groups.kicker: review-pr gives P3 entries to publish; fix-pr reads them with review suggestions
intro: The reviewer no longer writes a suggestions section. review-pr and method.md section 7 tell it to pass each P3 to publish as a threads-file entry, and they document the marker's new suggestions= field. fix-pr takes its suggestions from project review suggestions <number> --repo <owner>/<repo> and is told never to parse review bodies itself.

"Decide each suggestion" now runs project review suggestions.
